title: How do you build a training matrix for a telecommunications provider?
seoTitle: Training matrix for a telecom provider
description: Build a telecom training matrix: CPNI handling, NIS2 board and staff cyber training, card security, privacy duties by role and market, with a worked grid.
shortAnswer: A telecommunications provider builds its training matrix by separating the people who touch customer records (retail, care, sales, agents) from those who run and secure the network and those who govern it, then mapping each group to the customer data, cybersecurity and payment rules of every market it serves. Each cell states the trigger or interval, who signs off, and the record that supports the provider's certifications and incident duties.
keyTakeaways: Telecom training duties fall into three families: customer data handling (such as CPNI in the United States), network and information security (NIS2 in the EU), and payment card and privacy rules.

Few telecom rules set an interval. PCI DSS requires the awareness program to be reviewed every 12 months, and the CPNI officer certification is annual, but CPNI and NIS2 training clocks are left to the provider.
Management bodies carry personal duties: NIS2 Article 20(2) requires them to follow cybersecurity training, and Portugal makes ensuring regular training a non delegable duty of the board.
Agents, affiliates and suppliers belong in the matrix because CPNI handling and NIS2 awareness programs extend beyond employees.
As at November 2026, Portugal's Decree-Law 125/2025 is in force with some training measures deferred, and the FCC's SIM change training rule awaits a compliance date.

sections.heading: Why does a telecom provider's matrix look different from a typical IT matrix?

blocks.text: Because a telecom provider is regulated both as a holder of sensitive customer records and as an operator of infrastructure that others depend on, and each role sits differently across those two regimes. A retail store employee who can view a subscriber's call details has duties under customer data rules that a network engineer does not, while the engineer falls under cybersecurity risk management rules that barely touch the store.

The method in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) still applies. What a telecom provider adds is a data access attribute on each role (whether it can see customer proprietary information, cardholder data or network systems) so that columns attach automatically. This is a practical form of [role based training](/glossary/role-based-training).

sections.heading: Which telecom roles should form the rows?

blocks.text: Group roles by what they can access and what they sign, because that is how the rules allocate duties. The table lists typical rows and the rules behind them.

sections.heading: Which training rules apply to telecom providers in each market?

blocks.text: Pull columns from the regulation pages for each market where the provider holds customers or operates network assets. Each summary uses only the linked page.

items: **United States.** The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) requires telecommunications carriers, including interconnected VoIP providers, to train personnel on when they are and are not authorized to use customer proprietary network information (CPNI) and to have an express disciplinary process under 47 CFR 64.2009(b) ([FCC CPNI training](/regulations/fcc-cpni-employee-training-requirements)). An officer signs a compliance certificate filed on or before March 1 for the previous calendar year. Section 64.2010 sets authentication rules for phone, online and in store access, and 64.2011 requires notice to the US Secret Service and FBI no later than seven business days after a breach is reasonably determined.

**European Union.** NIS2 Article 20(2) requires members of management bodies of essential and important entities to follow training, and Member States encourage similar regular training for employees; Article 21(2)(g) lists basic cyber hygiene and cybersecurity training as a required measure ([NIS2](/regulations/nis2-management-body-training)). Digital infrastructure is among the sectors in scope. Implementing Regulation 2024/2690 describes an awareness program covering management bodies and suppliers, testing of its effectiveness, role training with effectiveness assessed, and training on transfer. GDPR adds the data protection officer's duty to monitor training and the rule that people with access to personal data act only on instructions ([GDPR staff training](/regulations/gdpr-staff-training-requirements)).

**Portugal.** Decree-Law 125/2025 transposes NIS2 ([Portugal cybersecurity law](/regulations/portugal-cybersecurity-law-training)). Regime Article 25(1)(d) requires management bodies to ensure regular cybersecurity training, with liability for intent or gross negligence, and the duty cannot be delegated except to a member. Article 27(1)(f) lists cyber hygiene and training for top management and workers, and Article 31 has the cybersecurity officer propose training. The decree also revokes the security articles 59 to 65 of the Electronic Communications Law, Law 16/2022, with delayed effect.

**United Arab Emirates.** The Information Assurance Regulation published by the Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA) is mandatory for government entities and entities designated critical under the CIIP Policy, whose scope includes the ICT sector ([UAE information assurance](/regulations/uae-information-assurance-awareness-training)). Its M3 family requires a documented training needs analysis, which is a P1 Always Applicable control, plus a program, effectiveness evaluation and training records.

**Any market with card sales.** PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.6 requires a security awareness program for all personnel, reviewed at least every 12 months, with training on phishing, social engineering and acceptable use of end user technologies, mandatory since 31 March 2025 ([PCI DSS](/regulations/pci-dss-security-awareness-training-requirements)).

sections.heading: Where do telecom rules fix a frequency, and where must the provider decide?

blocks.text: Telecom rules mostly require that training exist and work, not that it recur on a schedule. The provider sets most clocks itself and must be able to explain why.

items: **Fixed by rule.** The PCI DSS awareness program is reviewed at least once every 12 months. The CPNI compliance certificate is filed annually by March 1. Portuguese significant incidents require initial notification within 24 hours and an update within 72 hours, which training for incident handlers should reflect.
**Required but untimed.** CPNI training under 64.2009(b), NIS2 management body training, Portuguese regular training under Article 25 and UAE M3 training all leave frequency open.

**Event triggers.** Implementing Regulation 2024/2690 includes training when staff transfer roles. The FCC requires written notice within five business days when opt out mechanisms fail beyond an anomaly, a natural trigger for refresher training of the teams involved.

**Documenting the choice.** Write the reason for each chosen interval beside the cell. The approach is set out in [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: What records should a telecom provider keep to back its training?

blocks.text: Keep records that support the provider's certifications and incident reports, because those are where training evidence is tested. A completion list alone will not support an officer's signed CPNI certificate.

items: **CPNI.** Sales campaign and disclosure records and compliance records are kept at least one year; breach records at least two years.
**NIS2.** Implementing Regulation 2024/2690 expects effectiveness of awareness programs to be tested and role training effectiveness to be assessed, so keep test results, not only attendance.

**UAE.** M3.2.1 sub controls require records of education, training, skills, experience and qualifications, and M4.3 uses the percentage of employees who took security awareness training as an indicator.

**Board reporting.** Because NIS2 and Portuguese law place training duties on the management body, report coverage and effectiveness to it directly. See [how to report training compliance to the board](/guides/how-to-report-training-compliance-to-the-board) and the country comparison of [cybersecurity awareness training requirements](/compare/cybersecurity-awareness-training-requirements-by-country).

sections.heading: Which telecom training changes should be tracked into 2027?

blocks.text: Several telecom items are dated or pending. As at November 2026, the linked regulation pages record the following:

items: **3 April 2026, Portugal:** Decree-Law 125/2025 entered into force, 120 days after its 4 December 2025 publication.

**24 months after implementing regulations, Portugal:** Article 27(1) and (2) measures, including the cyber hygiene and training measure, take effect 24 months after publication of the regulations listed in Article 10(2). Track that trigger rather than a fixed date.
**1 March 2027, United States:** the next annual CPNI compliance certificate, covering calendar year 2026, is due.
**Pending, United States:** 47 CFR 64.2010(h)(7) requires SIM change fraud training, but (h)(9) states compliance is not required until a compliance date is added.
**Pending, EU:** the Commission's January 2026 proposal COM(2026) 13 would make targeted NIS2 amendments; it is not yet law.

blocks.title: Breach notice amendment
blocks.text: The CPNI breach notification amendment published at 89 FR 10002 on 12 February 2024 was shown as not yet incorporated in the eCFR at the date of the CPNI regulation page. Confirm the current text before rewriting breach training.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each telecom obligation to the roles and access types it attaches to, and to the learning outcomes and assessment points that evidence it, so the data behind a CPNI certificate or a NIS2 board report traces back to its rule. When a regulation such as the Portuguese cybersecurity regime adds a compliance date, the affected roles are flagged. See [knowledge governance](/platform/knowledge-governance).

faqs.q: Do interconnected VoIP providers need CPNI training?
faqs.a: Yes. 47 CFR 64.2003(o) treats an entity providing interconnected VoIP service as a carrier for CPNI purposes, so the training duty in 64.2009(b) and the annual officer certificate apply. The matrix should include VoIP customer care and sales roles on the same basis as traditional carrier staff.

faqs.q: Does NIS2 require every telecom employee to be trained?
faqs.a: Article 20(2) requires management body members to follow training and asks Member States to encourage similar training for employees, while Article 21(2)(g) makes cybersecurity training a required risk management measure. National laws then set the detail: in Portugal, Article 27(1)(f) names training for top management and workers.

faqs.q: Is CPNI training the same as privacy training?
faqs.a: No. CPNI rules focus on when personnel may use specific network information, such as numbers called and when, and how customers are authenticated. General privacy training under GDPR or other privacy laws covers wider personal data duties. Keep separate columns, though one module can cover both if the mapping is recorded.

faqs.q: Should field and network contractors appear in the matrix?
faqs.a: Yes, where they handle customer information or fall within the security program. NIS2 awareness programs under Implementing Regulation 2024/2690 extend to suppliers, and CPNI rules cover agents and affiliates acting for the carrier. Give contractors their own rows with the obligations their access triggers.
